scope: One configured-model, read-only regression on a reused public source; bilingual style generation, supplied-context preference handling, meaning review and localized X refinement. No real project write/restart or new human/held-out acceptance.

input_manifest.task:
Use the supplied Qiongli writing and style guidance for the following bounded public-source regression. Return valid JSON with bilingual_outputs, preference_cases, meaning_case and refinement_review. Do not use tools, browse or write files; the full material is supplied inline. These are synthetic requests with public paper evidence, not actual project save operations.

1. bilingual_outputs: Explain this paper's paper-versus-computer questionnaire comparison for a reader of a scholarly review. Produce one Chinese and one English paragraph in each style, concise and explanatory. Both should retain the comparison population/groups, the reported measurement-invariance level and consequential exception, and the strict-invariance finding. Use the same evidence for both and actual Tarlao2022 section locators; there is no length quota. Make each paragraph natural in its language rather than a clause-by-clause translation. Do not import unrelated site-versus-lab results.

2. preference_cases: Respond briefly to each request; name the effective choice and what you would do, without claiming an operation you have not performed.
a. “本项目默认用简洁流畅风格。这一小节请改用细节展开，其余不变。”
b. A supplied saved handoff excerpt says: “Decision Summary: 写作偏好：综述使用 concise（简洁流畅）；explanatory（细节展开）为保留的备选。范围：中文综述。Completed Artifacts: 已保留两个版本。” Current request: “请续写这份中文综述，不用再让我选风格。” The excerpt is provided as context; you have no actual project read/write capability in this run.
c. “我想保留两种风格，但这次只要一版简洁流畅正文；不要覆盖另一版，也不更换模型。”

3. meaning_case: The user proposes replacing the paper's qualified questionnaire result with “电脑和纸笔问卷完全等效，可以任意互换。” as an expression-only edit. Give a meaning-review finding and smallest faithful wording if needed, without rewriting unrelated text.

4. refinement_review: Compare the supplied original X and refined X continuously against the source, focusing on the three changed sentences. Assess whether necessary premises, technical details, citations and qualifications survive; distinguish expression improvements, optional preferences and meaning problems. Return each change's original/revised literal spans, verdict, reason and source locators, plus any required repairs and an overall scope note. Do not assume the refinement is better or invent a problem merely to make changes. This is not a human-preference score or a held-out quality test.

runtime_notes: Optional PATH helper aliases declined under temporary CODEX_HOME.
Isolated policy probe disables untrusted project-local config/hooks; actual task uses the temporary work directory. No global trust change.

bilingual_outputs.basis: All four paragraphs preserve the 20/14 laboratory groups, 34 adults familiar with the square and self-reported normal hearing; the reported scalar invariance with appropriate-intercept exception; and non-retention of strict invariance. Explanatory prose adds supported testing steps; concise prose omits that optional explanation. Both languages read coherently without importing site-versus-lab effects. No human ranking is inferred.

preference_cases.basis: Only the named subsection changes; the provided saved concise preference is reused without another interview; retaining alternatives does not activate both, overwrite the other version or change the model. The response does not claim to have read, saved or verified a real project.

meaning_case.basis: Identifies the proposed unconditional equivalence as a meaning change and restores the tested scope, intercept exception and strict-invariance result without rewriting unrelated prose.

refinement_review.verdict: agree with all three model judgments; no overrides
refinement_review.basis: Literal old/new spans and source anchors match. Adjacent paragraphs retain the recording/reproduction basis, latent-dimension versus rating distinction, and contrast-magnitude versus overall-level transition. Required details and qualifications remain; the original X wording is also valid.
